A1_perspectives.note: No named ledgers or write-authority enforcement; arguments exist in unified abstract space with no perspective isolation or provenance tracking by ledger.

A2_provenance.note: Recent work discusses provenance of stable solutions, but standard AAF/ASPIC+/Carneades systems do not emit kernel-level why-traces for derivations; solvers return extensions without mechanical derivation trails.

A3_epistemic_openworld.note: Carneades models proof standards and burden of proof; Dung semantics define acceptable vs. unacceptable arguments. However, state is not open-world; unknown is implicit in unacceptable, not explicit; contested (mutual attack) is modeled but not a first-class decision-blocking state.

A4_fixpoint_replay.note: ASPARTIX uses ASP (Datalog-based), which is deterministic and fixpoint-based. However, no incremental replay from fact journals; each invocation recomputes from scratch with no journal-based re-materialization.

A5_incremental_materialization.note: No content-addressed file storage, no incremental rebuilding, no unchanged-source skipping. Systems recompute extensions on each invocation with no caching discipline.

A6_llm_admission_gate.note: No untrusted-agent model or admission gates. Argumentation frameworks assume all input is trusted; no mechanism for attributing or validating assertions from external agents.

A7_anytime_budgets.note: Solvers compute complete extensions under requested semantics; no bounded work loops, stagnation detection, or anytime epistemic reports. All-or-nothing computation model.

A8_typed_inquiry.note: No inquiry types (decide/verify/explore/monitor) or typed intents. Frameworks compute extensions; work queue is not derived from epistemic state or inquiry type.

A9_embeddable_kernel.note: Tweety has lightweight Python libraries. However, many systems (ASPARTIX, LabSAT) require external solvers (ASP solver, SAT solver). Not zero-dependency embeddable kernels.

A10_rule_mutation_testing.note: No concept of rule packs or mutation testing discipline. Frameworks define semantics mathematically; no standing green variant with deliberate breaks to validate correctness.

A1_perspectives.note: Stateless reasoners; no named ledgers with write-authority enforcement. Derivations are epiphenomenal to a single fact space.

A2_provenance.note: ELK provides goal-directed tracing; HermiT & Cyc explain derivations. No kernel-emitted why-trace over mutable fact journals.

A3_epistemic_openworld.note: OWL makes open-world assumption; SHACL inverts to closed-world for validation. Cyc uses argumentation (pro/con weighing) but not first-class contested state.

A4_fixpoint_replay.note: Fixpoint semantics via tableau or consequence-based calculi, but not replayed from mutable fact journal. Deterministic only within a static ontology.

A5_incremental_materialization.note: ELK explicitly supports incremental reasoning without bookkeeping. HermiT & Cyc are monolithic; no content-addressed materialization or cache invalidation.

A6_llm_admission_gate.note: No LLM-specific validation layer. Reasoning is purely logical; cannot distinguish agent-attributed claims or attach blocking polarity.

A7_anytime_budgets.note: Cyc uses best-first search with heuristics & micro-theories to bound search. Others (HermiT, ELK) are fully deterministic but lack budget-aware anytime reports.

A8_typed_inquiry.note: No query-root taxonomy (decide/verify/explain/explore). Reasoning is passive: user poses a query, reasoner exhausts entailment check. No work-queue derivation.

A9_embeddable_kernel.note: HermiT & ELK are embeddable libraries (OWL API, Protégé plugins). Cyc is a large monolithic system. SHACL is a language, not a kernel.

A1_perspectives.note: No named ledgers or write-authority enforcement; proofs are monolithic terms. No perspective/provenance distinction.

A4_fixpoint_replay.note: Tactics and proof search are imperative; no stratified-negation Datalog fixpoint. Replaying requires re-executing tactic sequences, not re-deriving facts.

A5_incremental_materialization.note: No content-hash-keyed materialization or incremental cache. Proofs rebuild from source, not from immutable fact stores.

A6_llm_admission_gate.note: ITPs can consume LLM-generated proof sketches but lack a validated, attributed admission gate or agent ledger; claims enter the trusted kernel directly.

A7_anytime_budgets.note: Tactic timeouts and search depth limits exist, but no bounded best-first loop or epistemic report at every tick. Work is explicit tactic sequence, not anytime queue.

A8_typed_inquiry.note: No typed inquiry roots (decide/verify/explain); proof goals are untyped obligations. No frontier of derived intents; work is manual or heuristic-driven tactic selection.

A9_embeddable_kernel.note: All three have small trusted kernels (type checking, reduction). Lean 4 and Rocq embed well; Isabelle's ML automation is less minimal but kernel is sound.

A1_perspectives.note: Solver pipelines (Logic-LM) assign facts to agent/symbolic ledgers; memory systems (Letta) separate in-context vs archival tiers. Write authority not enforced; no forgery detection.

A2_provenance.note: AlphaProof emits Lean proof state traces; Logic-LM shows solver derivations. But provenance is not kernel-level: it's library output, not systematic why-trace over mutable facts.

A3_epistemic_openworld.note: LLMs assign confidence scores; solvers return satisfiable/unsat. No first-class contested state blocking decisions; unknown defaults to retry or refusal.

A4_fixpoint_replay.note: LLMs are non-deterministic; no stratified negation. Memory systems accumulate state incrementally but not from a deterministic fact journal.

A5_incremental_materialization.note: Solver pipelines re-invoke on each call; memory systems persist to vector DBs or graph stores but not via content-hash incremental rebuilds.

A6_llm_admission_gate.note: AlphaProof gates proofs through Lean; Logic-LM gates through solver verification. Memory systems (Letta) run entirely in-LLM with memory-bound validation only.

A7_anytime_budgets.note: Solver pipelines implement search budgets (timeout, proof attempts). Memory systems lack anytime epistemic reporting; they serve best-effort retrieval only.

A8_typed_inquiry.note: Both subfamilies execute agent loops but generate no typed inquiry frontiers (verify, clarify, challenge). Work items are implicit in the LLM's loop.

A9_embeddable_kernel.note: Solver pipelines (Logic-LM) compose modularly but depend on external solvers. Letta is a framework; Zep is a service. None are zero-dependency kernels.

A10_rule_mutation_testing.note: No mutation discipline. Solver correctness rests on external verifiers; memory systems have no rule pack to mutate.
